title: NP-completeness of the hull number problem for oriented chordal graphs
statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph and let $k$ be a positive integer. The underlying graph of $D$ is the graph obtained by ignoring the orientations of its arcs.

**Oriented chordal hull-number conjecture.** Determining whether

$$
\overrightarrow{\operatorname{hn}}(D)\leq k
$$

is NP-complete, even when the underlying graph of $D$ is chordal.

This would extend the known NP-hardness of determining the hull number of an undirected chordal graph to oriented graphs. The source presents the claim as an open problem; its precise complexity for oriented graphs with chordal underlying graphs remains open.
source_name: Julio C. S. Araujo and Pedro S. M. Arraes, “Hull and Geodetic Numbers for Some Classes of Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:1911.10240 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10240
